A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 34-page versions of CONGO, including Appendices A-G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison; differences are confined to pages 1, 14, and 19.

before.justification: v3 reports original quadratic optimization experiments, Jackson network simulations, and DeathStarBench SocialNetwork evaluations in Sections 6-7, plus empirical analyses in Appendices E-F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their results in Sections 6-7 and Appendices E-F.

M1.justification: CONGO-B, CONGO-Z, and CONGO-E retain identical sampling, gradient recovery, and update procedures, including Algorithms 1-2. The mathematical corrections do not change the algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same sparse quadratic objectives, 15- and 50-queue Jackson networks, SocialNetwork workloads, and additional test scenarios in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GD and GDSP in Section 6; NSGD and SGDSP in Section 7.1; and NSGD, SGDSP, and PPO in Section 7.2, alongside the same CONGO variants.

E3.justification: Sample budgets, experimental horizons, cost metrics, workload schedules, and hyperparameters are unchanged in Sections 6-7 and Appendix G, including Tables 1-12.

E4.justification: Appendices E-F retain the same recovery-runtime comparison, measurement-count and gradient-limit analyses, sparsity robustness tests, and dimension-scaling experiments with a fixed sampling budget.

E5.justification: Both report 50 random seeds for the quadratic experiments, five seeds for Jackson simulations, and four runs for microservice trials. Averaging and standard-deviation reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Empirical curves, numerical findings, and rankings are identical throughout the main text and appendices. Section 7.2 retains the reported approximately 45% and 20% cost reductions; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: In Appendix A (page 14) and Appendix C.3.1 (page 19), v3 incorrectly gives both RIP bounds as (1 - δ_k)||x||_2^2. v4 changes the upper bound to (1 + δ_k)||x||_2^2. This corrects the mathematical property in the background and Lemma 2's proof; the remaining derivations and theorem statements are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparsity-based sampling efficiency, dimension-independent O(sqrt(T)) regret, and practical autoscaling benefits.

C2.justification: Explanations of algorithm performance and the limitations concerning exact sparsity, known parameter bounds, and queue stability are unchanged, including the appendix discussions.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware specifications, runtime information, and code-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with Borkar et al., ZORO, and prior microservice autoscaling systems. The RIP correction adds no citation or novelty claim.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 6 March 2025 to v4 dated 16 May 2025. Apart from this metadata update, prose, terminology, headings, and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-12 and Tables 1-12 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. The equation corrections and updated version stamp introduce no layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: Correcting the repeated RIP upper-bound sign removes an erroneous mathematical statement from Appendix A and Lemma 2's proof, making the inequalities consistent with approximate norm preservation. This is a limited improvement in correctness; the algorithms, theorem conclusions, and empirical evidence are otherwise unchanged.
